name: Pittsburgh Roaring Run RV Resort
note: 100-acre Laurel Highlands campground at 194 Tannery Rd, Champion, between the Seven Springs and Hidden Valley resorts and about 8 mi from Kooser State Park; RV Life counts 230 sites. Under its current owners it is open to the public - the site's own banner reads "RV Sites Available - No Membership Needed" - and is not the membership resort the Roaring Run name once carried. Nightly back-in RV sites with 30-amp electric, water, cable, picnic table and fire ring are published, with monthly and seasonal tiers, rustic cabins from $162 and tent sites also offered. Amenities include an Olympic-size pool, wading pool, camp store, game lodge, mini golf, tennis/basketball/volleyball courts and playgrounds. Satellite shows one large open RV oval of roughly 40 pads plus wooded loops and cabins. Booking is by phone (878-978-2408) or the site's request form; there is no online booking engine. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Book by phone ((878) 978-2408, also 724-593-7837) or the site's 'Book Now' request form; no online booking engine. 'RV Sites Available – No Membership Needed'. Monthly sites from $560 and full-season sites $3,000 (May-Nov 2026) are also sold.
field_notes.Fees: Pittsburgh Roaring Run: 30-amp water/electric back-ins $45 Sunday-Thursday, $50 Friday and Saturday; the pricing page lists $60 nightly. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Potter County Family Campground
note: Privately owned (the operator says so explicitly) 44-acre wooded park at 3075 E 2nd St on US 6 at the top of Denton Hill, 8 mi east of Coudersport across from the State Police barracks - despite the name it is not a county park. 105 campsites including 15 camping cabins; the operator's campground-map PDF shows numbered water/electric and water/electric/sewer drive-in pads (sites 1-105) on two long loops off the access road, plus primitive tent sites, heated bathhouses with private showers, camp store, dump station, honey-wagon service and a rentable pavilion. 2026 nightly rates $35 primitive, cabins $58-128. The operator says it is open year-round (its April 1 - September 30 dates are for the rental camper only); direct access to the state ATV and snowmobile trail systems (ATV trails Memorial Day weekend to the last full weekend in September). Online booking through ResNexus. --Claude

Fees: +$5/night each person over 2 adults and 2 children

field_notes.Season: The operator says 'Open Year Round!' (heated bathhouses, snowmobile trail access). Its April 1 - September 30 dates are for the rental camper only.
field_notes.Booking: Online booking through ResNexus. A one-night deposit is due at booking and is nonrefundable; cancellations must be made more than 7 days ahead or the full stay is charged.
field_notes.Fees: 2026 rates for 2 adults and 2 children: water/electric site $40 a night, full hookup $45 (primitive tent site $35). Extra adults $5 a night; air conditioner or electric heater use $3 a day; optional $5 lock fee to guarantee a site number. Deposit of one night, nonrefundable; cancellations under 7 days pay in full. Read 2026-10-20.
field_notes.Sites: The operator gives 105 campsites including 15 camping cabins; the 90 others include primitive tent sites.

name: Wilsonville Recreation Area
note: Largest of the Lake Wallenpaupack recreation areas, on a wooded point off US 6 at 113 Ammon Dr; the lake and its recreation areas are owned and run by utility operator Brookfield Renewable (formerly PPL), so it is a utility park rather than a government one. 160 tent and trailer sites with camp store, showers, laundry, dump station, playground, marina with rental slips, gas dock and boat ramps. The operator's colour site map classes sites as seasonal, 7-night-minimum, or 2-night-minimum (3 nights on holidays), so a large transient block is bookable; seasonal sites are currently full. 2026 rates $38 tent, 15% off at 30+ nights, 30-night maximum stay. Camping season runs the last Sunday in April to the third Sunday in October. Electric and water reach at least part of the loop (a dated firsthand review reports 30A and water at site 41). No online booking - mail-in reservation form from Jan 1, phone reservations from Apr 25. No pets permitted, and swimming is not allowed within the recreation area. The older wilsonvillecampground.com domain now serves an expired certificate; wilsonvillecampground1.com is the live site. --Claude MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on reservations (7 at some sites), 3 on summer holiday weekends; first-come stays from 1 night (wilsonvillecampground1.com, 2026-10-12). --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights, 3 on holidays (Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends)
Fees: +$10/night each adult over 2, each child over 2 $5

field_notes.Season: Camping season: the last Sunday in April to the third Sunday in October.
field_notes.Booking: Reservations: 2 nights or more at some sites, 7 or more at others, 3 over the Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends; first-come camping for 1 to 30 nights (operator's rules). No online or email booking: mail-in form from January 1, phone from April 25 (570-226-4382). Deposit one night (half for 30 nights, holidays paid in full); reservations held until 9 PM on arrival day. The camping page gives a $25 cancellation fee, the rules page $10.
field_notes.Fees: RVs and trailers $45 a night, $50 on holidays (3-night minimum); tents $38/$43; 15% off at 30+ nights on designated sites. Covers two adults and two children; extra children $5, adults $10. Boat launch $10 per stay. Read 2026-10-20.

name: Sunvalley Campground
note: Formerly Longview Campground, same property at 7570 Robinson Road at the base of Cove Mountain in the Tuscarora range. Operator's own campground map shows 88 numbered drive-in sites - 30-amp water/electric, 50-amp, sewer and frost-free sewer classes - plus lettered primitive tent sites, two playgrounds, pool and pavilion; directory listings put it at 87 sites (18 full hookup, 69 water/electric) taking rigs to 43 ft. Reservations by phone only, no online booking; open roughly May through October, with a Haunted Trail run in the fall. Caveat: the operator's site still carries a stale 2022-2024 winter-closure line and a 2023 copyright, but the park is demonstrably operating - a July 2025 RV Life review describes friendly staff, a clean park, camp store and firewood on site. RV Life ~$38/night. --Claude

field_notes.Sites: The operator's map numbers 88 drive-in sites (30-amp water/electric, 50-amp, sewer and frost-free sewer classes) besides five primitive tent sites and three lettered sites; it gives no lengths.

name: Rafter J Bar Ranch Camping Resort
note: Large private resort 3 mi south of Hill City off US-16/385 on Rafter J-Bar Rd, backing onto Black Hills National Forest and the Mickelson Trail. 200 sites in six camping areas (Main, Base, Ranch, Lower Ranch, The Island, Line) plus a separate cabin camp: 30/50 amp, back-ins, concrete-pad deluxe patio sites, pool and hot tub, bathhouses and playground. $20 to request a specific site. Online booking was refusing reservations in Sept 2026 ("please call us directly") - phone to book.

Fees: +$5/night each adult over 2, children 10 and under free

field_notes.Booking: The online reservation page was refusing bookings in Sept 2026 ("please call us directly to book your stay"); phone the office.
field_notes.Fees: The operator publishes no nightly rate table, so no base rate is recorded here; RV Life's average was $67/night in 9/2026. Extras that are published: $6 reservation fee, $20/day per additional vehicle or ATV (advance booking, gravel pad only), $20 to request a specific site, rates cover 2 people and $5/night for each additional person over age 10.

name: North Fruita Desert Campground (18 Road)
note: BLM (Grand Junction Field Office) campground at the 18 Road (North Fruita Desert) mountain-bike trail system, ~7-8.5 mi north of Fruita at the foot of the Book Cliffs, among scattered juniper with wide views of the Grand Valley. Ride to the trails from the campsites; the Lower Campground doubles as an event staging area. Hot in summer, sparse shade. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reservations are required for all camping. Sites A1-A14, B1-B12, G1-G23, H1-H5, J5-J7, K8-K15 and the group sites book up to six months ahead; C, D, E, F, J1-J4 and K1-K7 open only four days before arrival. Changes until 24 hours before; you cannot change the check-in date.
field_notes.Fees: $20 a site, up to 10 people and 2 vehicles; group sites (D9, D11, G24) $40-50. $8 non-refundable reservation fee per reservation. Same rates all year in recreation.gov's 2024-2028 tables.
field_notes.Sites: Two units 1.5 mi apart on 18 Road: the Upper Campground (58 sites incl. group sites D9, D11; graveled spurs, no tent pads) and the Lower Campground (53 sites incl. group site G24, 12x12 tent pads) at the trailhead and event staging area, where some sites may close during races and festivals. Site sizes vary - check the dimensions before booking; many pull-throughs, a few spurs as short as 20 ft. 10 people and 2 vehicles a site.

name: Cooper Creek Campground
note: Chattahoochee NF campground on Cooper Creek in the North Georgia mountains, off GA-60 south of Morganton (Blue Ridge Ranger District); known for year-round trout fishing. Two loops booked together: Cooper Creek (sites 12-25, with 15-16 on the creek) and Mulky (sites 1-11), about 700 m apart. Reservable online; no hookups; no cell coverage. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Open all year; water and full rates April-October, reduced off-peak rate November-March.
field_notes.Booking: Mulky Loop (sites 1-11) is booked under this campground. Two vehicles per site except group site 24. No cell coverage.
field_notes.Fees: Standard sites $15 a night in peak season (Apr 1-Oct 31), $7.50 off-peak (Nov 1-Mar 31, water shut off). Group site 24 $30 / $15. Same rates loaded through 2028.
field_notes.Sites: 25 sites in two loops: Cooper Creek (12-25) and Mulky (1-11). 22 take an RV: tent-only 6 and 12 are out, and site 7's driveway is 10 ft; group site 24 included. Driveways 36-99 ft; site 23 is the RV pull-through. Creek sites 15 and 16.

name: Upper Chattahoochee River Campground
note: Chattahoochee NF campground at the headwaters of the Chattahoochee River, 5 miles up gravel Forest Service Road 44 (Upper Chattahoochee River Road) off GA-75 north of Helen. No ATVs, UTVs or golf carts on the campground or the road.  ONLY TWO SITES FIT: sites 15 and 16 are the only ones recreation.gov lets a 23-ft rig book (trailers with no length limit); the rest cap trailers at 10-16 ft or allow no trailer at all, so book one of those two (2026-10-30). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reservation only, online or at 877-444-6777, made before coming to the site. 14 nights in any 30 days on Chattahoochee-Oconee NF land, then leave the forest for 30 days. Check-in 2 pm, check-out 12:01 pm.
field_notes.Sites: 19 sites, but recreation.gov permits no RV or motorhome type on any of them and caps trailers at 10 ft on 13 sites (site 1: 14 ft, site 12: 16 ft); sites 13-14 take pickup campers and pop-ups to 14 ft but no trailer; sites 9-11 are tent sites. Only sites 15 and 16 (parallel pull-offs, driveways 41 and 39 ft) permit a trailer with no length limit, so 2 is the count a 23-ft motorhome can book.

name: Mill Run Recreation Area (Youghiogheny River Lake)
note: USACE campground on the Mill Run arm of Youghiogheny River Lake in the Laurel Highlands, just north of the Maryland line off Route 40 via Friendsville-Addison Road and Mill Run Road. 30 sites, several right on the cove; flush toilets, drinking water, dump station, beach, boat launch, playground; no hookups. Reservable online; holiday weekends must be booked Friday-Sunday. Site length not published - ring the Youghiogheny project office before bringing a 23-ft rig. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reserve on recreation.gov or (877) 444-6777; information (814) 395-3242. Holiday weekends must be booked for the whole weekend, Friday through Sunday, with no refund for leaving early. 14 nights in any 30 consecutive days at the project. Maximum two tents, or one tent and one trailer, per site.
field_notes.Fees: Every site is a standard non-electric site at $20 a night (recreation.gov rate tables 2024-2027).
field_notes.Sites: 30 reservable standard non-electric sites, every one back-in; recreation.gov publishes no max vehicle length for any of them.

name: AuSable River Campsites - Alcona Pond
note: Six drive-in sites strung over about 1.5 km below Alcona Dam Pond; pick 001D, 002D, 003D or 006D (26 ft) for a 23-ft rig. Part of the AuSable River Dispersed Camping system: 102 designated sites along 55 miles of the lower AuSable in the Huron NF, booked as one recreation.gov facility. Dirt or gravel parking aprons; the sites sit on bluffs 5-300 ft above the river and access to the water can be steep. Equipment within 25 ft of the site post; two vehicles and two camping units per site. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Open all year, but not maintained December 1 - April 14.
field_notes.Booking: Run directly by the Forest Service (Huron Shores Ranger District), not a concessionaire. Every site is reserved by number on recreation.gov April 15 - November 30; December 1 - April 14 no permit or reservation is required. Occupy the site within 24 hours of the reservation's start or it is forfeit unless the Forest Service approves a late arrival. 14 nights in any 30 days.
field_notes.Fees: $10 a night per single site April 15 - November 30 (the same in every rate season through 2028 on recreation.gov); December 1 - April 14 no permit or reservation is required and recreation.gov's first-come season carries a $0 fee.
field_notes.Sites: Six drive-in sites 001D-004D and 006D-007D, all back-in, for tent, RV or trailer: 001D, 002D, 003D and 006D to 26 ft, 004D and 007D to 18 ft. The section's seventh site, 005C, is a tent-only boat-in.

name: Gypsum Campground (Eagle River, BLM)
note: BLM (Colorado River Valley FO) campground on the Eagle River just off I-70 Exit 140 at Gypsum: turn south, then right on the frontage road (Old Highway 6) 1.5 miles past the roundabout. Gravel loops between the interstate and the river; a trail leads to the river for fishing and raft access (floating late May-July). Reviewers fit 24-30 ft rigs; the sites further up the road are the better ones. Constant I-70 noise. --Claude

field_notes.Sites: BLM gives no site count or length limit. Listings say 8 sites; campers report 24-30 ft rigs fitting. Imagery shows two gravel loops with back-in spurs.

name: Hall Valley Campground (Webster Pass Road)
note: Small Forest Service campground at 9,900 ft off Park County Road 60, north of US-285 at Webster toward Red Cone and Webster passes (four-wheel-drive routes beyond the campground). Only the longer parking spurs fit a 23-ft rig. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Full service Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day weekend; an extended season follows when water, trash or a host may not be available. All dates weather dependent.
field_notes.Booking: Strictly first-come. Pay cash, check or money order on site, or by recreation.gov Scan and Pay.
field_notes.Fees: $24 a site (two vehicles or one RV); $11 a third vehicle. Senior/Access passes halve the site fee.
field_notes.Sites: Parking spurs 16-30 ft, so only some sites take a 23-ft rig. Two tents and two vehicles, or one RV, per site.

name: Pierz City Park Campground
note: City campground in Pierz, east of Little Falls. 38 sites, all with water and electric (15 held for seasonal campers); bathrooms, showers, dump station. Reservations online through Campspot (as Pierz Golf Course and Campground) or by phone. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Campspot quote for Tue 6 - Wed 7 July 2027, 2 adults: electric and water RV site $53 a night (36 of 36 free, rigs to 50 ft). The park books online as Pierz Golf Course and Campground.

name: Deep Creek Campground (Green Lane Park)
note: Montgomery County campground in Green Lane Park by the Green Lane Reservoir. Wooded sites with no hookups and no dump station; bath house with showers. RVs to 25 ft. Open April 1 to October 30; book online, same day allowed until the gate closes at sunset; 14-night limit per season. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Booked on the county's Green Lane Park reservations site; same-day reservations online, but not after the gate closes at sunset. The 14-night maximum is per camping season. No refunds, credits or rain dates.
field_notes.Fees: $22/campsite/night for Montgomery County residents, $34 non-county residents.

name: Lake Towhee Park Campground
note: Bucks County park near Quakertown with 17 rustic family sites (no electric or water) by a small lake. Comfort station with shower mid-April to mid-November; dump station for campers. Motorhomes to 25 ft, trailers to 18 ft. Reserve online; 14-day limit. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Sites 15-17 in the main park: 'Camping is available year round'; the comfort station and shower close November 15 - April 15 (portable toilets then).
field_notes.Booking: Reserve through Bucks County's rec1 catalog (account needed) or call 215-757-0571. Rentals are accepted only for the current calendar year. Check-in after 3 pm, check-out before 2 pm; written cancellation 7 business days ahead.
field_notes.Fees: Family campsites $25 a day per site for Bucks County residents, $50 for non-residents; group camping $5 / $10 a person a day. Card payments carry a $1.50 to 2.35% convenience fee; $10 cancellation fee.
field_notes.Sites: 17 family sites and 2 group sites; family sites 1, 3, 4, 5, 9, 11, 12, 15, 16 and 17 'will allow for an RV 25ft or less, a trailer 18ft or less, or two tents' (the rest are tent sites). One unit per site, 2 vehicles, up to 6 people. Sites 15-17 are in the main park.

name: James Dykes Memorial Park (Dykes Landing)
note: Bleckley County boat landing on the Ocmulgee River off Porter Road near Cochran. First-come camping for RVs and trailers on the gravel landing - room for a few rigs; pavilion and picnic tables, but no water or restrooms. County ordinance limits stays to 7 nights in any 31 days.  CAVEAT: this is the boat landing itself - no marked campsites, water or toilets; you camp on the open gravel beside boaters' trailers (2026-10-30). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: County ordinance: overnight stays limited to 7 days in a 31-day period and 21 days in any 12 months; RVs and trailers must be registered and roadworthy. The ordinance describes no reservation or permit, so camping is on arrival.

name: Kinser Park
note: Greene County park near Greeneville on the Nolichucky River (Davy Crockett Lake), with pool, mini golf, ballfields and a boat ramp. About 130 RV sites, most full hookup; showers, dump station. Cash only per a 2025 review; some full-time residents share the campground, so call ahead for a transient site. Pad lengths not published. --Claude  CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $55 a night, cash, in July 2025 (Campendium review); the park has no web page, only a Facebook page (2026-10-11). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: A Campendium reviewer paid $55 a night in July 2025, cash only. No operator rate page (the park posts on Facebook only); confirm by phone.

name: Esofea/Rentz Memorial Park
note: Vernon County's oldest park, in a Driftless valley on the North Fork Bad Axe River near Westby. 10 full-hookup and 7 water/electric sites plus rustic sites; trout pond, 3 miles of trails. Reserve ahead (2-night minimum); April 15-October 15. --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on advance reservations; unreserved sites are first-come (Vernon County, 2026-10-12). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Advance reservations need 2 nights; online booking closes 3 days before arrival, and from each Wednesday unreserved sites are first-come for that weekend (Vernon County park page and 2024 rates and rules).
field_notes.Fees: Vernon County 2024 rate sheet (the one the park page links): rustic $20, electric and water $40, full hookup $45 a night; a week is 7 nights for the price of 6; $7 reservation fee. Advance reservations need 2 nights.

name: Trailway Campground
note: City of Montague campground on Business 31 between Montague and Whitehall, across the street from White Lake and beside the White River, the World's Largest Weathervane and the paved Hart-Montague bike trail; an easy walk to both downtowns. No boats or boat trailers overnight in the campground (paid parking in the adjacent city lot, arranged with the manager). About 30 of the roughly 55 sites are seasonal (2024 campground map). --Claude

Fees: +$5/night each adult over 2, children 15 and under free

field_notes.Booking: Reservations recommended: request one by phone (231-894-4903) or email (campground@cityofmontague.org), giving dates, RV type and length; email only in the off-season (Oct 15 - May 1). A deposit of half the camping fee is due within 7 days; cancellations more than 14 days out are refunded less a $30 processing fee, later ones forfeit the deposit. Specific sites are not guaranteed.
field_notes.Fees: RVs $50 a night, $300 a week, $900 a month plus electric; seasonal sites $3,600 plus electric for 5.5 months. One rate for everyone (no resident discount posted). Rates cover two adults and their children under 16; extra adults and children 16+ are $5 per person per night. Tents $25 (rustic area only).
field_notes.Sites: No tent sites (small tents in the rustic area as space allows). The 2024 campground map marks pull-through and back-in sites and about 30 seasonal sites. One RV and one vehicle per site; sites are assigned by management.

name: Shell Rock Recreation Area
note: Butler County Conservation area on the west edge of Shell Rock, between the Shell Rock River and a fishing pond, with boat and canoe access, a prairie and a playground. The reservable sites have gravel pads; the first-come sites are on grass and some share an electric post with the next site. --Claude

field_notes.Season: May 1 to October 15, weather permitting; the campground may open earlier and stay open later, with water and the shower house shut off in cold weather and self-registration only (no online reservations) outside the season.
field_notes.Booking: Only sites 03-06 book online, up to a year ahead and at least 7 days ahead, with a two-night minimum on weekend reservations; an unreserved reservable site can be taken first come, paid online only. All other sites are first come, first served, held by placing a unit and paying at once. Check-in after 3 pm, check-out by 2 pm. After 14 nights campers must leave for 3 nights.
field_notes.Fees: $20 a night at the first-come sites (grass pads, pay on site by QR code or cash envelope); $25 a night for the four online-reservable gravel-pad sites, plus a $4 processing fee per online reservation. Reservations are non-refundable.
field_notes.Sites: 23 public campsites on the county's booking listing (sites 03-06 reservable with gravel pads, sites 01-02 and 07-23 first-come with grass pads), plus a camp host site; the park page counts 27 electric posts, some shared by two sites, and several tent areas.

name: Hoisington RV Park
note: City of Hoisington RV sites in a row along the east edge of the asphalt parking lot behind the activity center (1200 Susank Rd) on the north edge of town; dump station on the north side of the lot. Self-register and pay at the drop box. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $20 a night in July 2025 and May 2026 (Campendium); the city's listing gives no rate. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Camper-reported: $20 a night (Campendium reports of July 2025 and May 2026), self-pay. The city's own listing gives only the address and phone.

name: Greensburg RV Park
note: Small privately run RV park on US-54 (W Kansas Ave) on the west side of downtown Greensburg: gravel pull-throughs behind the laundry building, a short walk to the Big Well. No signage and no website; call ahead. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $30 a night in May-September 2026 (RV Life reviews); the town's tourism listing still says $20. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Camper-reported: RV Life reviewers paid $30 a night in May, August and September 2026 (and October 2025) for full-hookup pull-throughs; the town's tourism listing still says $20 with weekly and monthly rates. The park has no web page of its own. Pay by self-pay envelope in the laundry room.

name: Alma RV Park (City Park)
note: City of Alma RV park at the edge of downtown, on a rise above the marshy west end of Harlan County Lake; open water is about 1 km south across the flats. Mostly seasonal: on the city's 2021 map 28 of 38 spaces are seasonal and 9 are transient. Wi-Fi is limited. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Only the transient spaces (9 of 38 on the 2021 map) are open to overnight campers, first come first served; the lease with the Corps of Engineers bars reservations for them. The other spaces are seasonal, filled by a lottery each fall.
field_notes.Fees: 2025 rates: $28/night including state sales and county lodging taxes; $165/week; $660/month.

name: Turner Falls Park RV Sites
note: City of Davis RV sites inside Turner Falls Park in the Arbuckle Mountains, off I-35. About 20 water/electric (50 amp) sites plus some 30 amp, dump station. PLUS daily park admission for every occupant; reservable online. No pets in the park. Very busy in summer. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: RV site permit $25/night PLUS park admission for every occupant (adults $16 weekday / $20 weekend in season).

name: Malin RV Park
note: City of Malin RV park in the Klamath Basin town near the California line, by the city pool. 11 full-hookup spaces, $125/week. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Full-hookup spaces $25/night ($125/week). From our own note (entry added 2026-09-28); not re-confirmed with the operator as of 2026-10-11.
